{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Target the existing Spring Cloud Data Flow codebase (Flo DSL parser, Spring Batch integration, Spring Cloud Deployer YARN SPI, Maven multi-module build) since the user stories reference Flo, SI, JobLaunchingTasklet, YARN SPI, and admin artifacts.",
    "U1: Extend the Flo DSL parser to accept 'timeout' and 'pollInterval' as global stream-level options, persist them in the stream definition metadata, and propagate them as deployment properties at runtime while keeping existing defaults for backward compatibility.",
    "U2: Perform the Spring Integration 4.2.1 upgrade through the central dependency management (Maven BOM), resolving any API/behavior changes and validating via the existing regression suite.",
    "U3: Profile JobLaunchingTasklet first to identify hot spots (e.g., redundant JobRepository lookups, repeated parameter conversion), then refactor internals without changing its public contract, keeping existing job-launch semantics intact.",
    "U4: Implement parameterized/data-driven tests that enumerate DSL variants and generated Spring XML configuration variants so both generation paths are covered by a shared test matrix.",
    "U5: Extend the stream definition DSL grammar to recognize inline SpEL expressions and evaluate them through a shared, hardened StandardEvaluationContext so the feature works uniformly for out-of-the-box and custom modules.",
    "U6: Author 'job orchestration' documentation in the existing Asciidoc reference guide, including composed batch workflow examples that use the DSL.",
    "U7: Add an UNDEPLOYED value to the YARN SPI deployment-state model and remap YARN application states so undeployed apps no longer surface as UNKNOWN; update status-conversion code and tests.",
    "U8: Restructure the build into a common admin core module plus per-Hadoop-distribution admin modules (e.g., HDP, CDH, PHD), each producing its own artifact with distro-scoped dependencies, and update CI/release packaging accordingly.",
    "Keep all changes backward compatible at the API and DSL level; no breaking changes to existing stream definitions or deployed streams."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "All work is performed by a single developer (the author) with no parallelization; estimates are effort, not elapsed duration.",
    "One workday equals 8 hours of focused development effort.",
    "A working development environment, Maven-based multi-module build, CI pipeline, and existing unit/integration test infrastructure are already in place.",
    "The generic Spring Framework 6.0 / Java 17 background text is contextual; the increment applies to the existing project line that uses Spring Integration 4.x, since U2 explicitly upgrades to SI 4.2.1.",
    "Per-activity estimates include design, implementation, and unit testing for that activity; cross-module integration/system testing and release activities are estimated as a separate activity.",
    "Documentation is written in the project's existing Asciidoc reference documentation; no separate publishing infrastructure work is required.",
    "Hadoop distribution verification is done against the three distros already referenced by the project (e.g., HDP, CDH, PHD) using existing test environments; no new infrastructure provisioning is included.",
    "Scope is limited to the eight user stories; project management, stakeholder meetings, and operational deployment work are excluded.",
    "The SpEL feature (U5) requires only inline expression support in stream definitions, not a general expression-authoring UI.",
    "No clarifying questions are needed; any ambiguity is resolved by the reasonable interpretations stated here."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Increment analysis and solution design",
      "activity_description": "Analyze the eight user stories, inspect the affected code areas (Flo DSL parser, SI dependencies, JobLaunchingTasklet, test infrastructure, YARN SPI, admin build), and produce the design for global DSL options, inline SpEL evaluation, YARN status mapping, and the per-distro admin module split.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "U1: Global timeout and pollInterval DSL options",
      "activity_description": "Implement global 'timeout' and 'pollInterval' options in the Flo DSL: parser/grammar changes, metadata storage, runtime propagation as deployment properties, default handling for backward compatibility, and unit tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 4
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "U2: Upgrade to Spring Integration 4.2.1",
      "activity_description": "Bump the Spring Integration version to 4.2.1 in dependency management, resolve dependency conflicts and API/behavior changes, adapt affected code, and run the regression suite to confirm stability.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "U3: Review and refactor JobLaunchingTasklet",
      "activity_description": "Review and profile JobLaunchingTasklet to identify performance bottlenecks, refactor internals (e.g., reduce redundant repository access and repeated conversions) while preserving behavior and public contract, and add/adjust unit and integration tests to validate the changes.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "U4: Test coverage for DSL and XML generation variants",
      "activity_description": "Define the variant matrix covering DSL constructs and generated XML configurations, implement parameterized tests exercising both generation paths, and stabilize the new tests within the existing test suite.",
      "most_likely_effort": 4
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "U5: Inline SpEL expressions in stream definitions",
      "activity_description": "Extend the stream definition DSL to support inline SpEL expressions: grammar/parser changes, evaluation via a shared hardened StandardEvaluationContext, validation and error handling, and tests covering out-of-the-box and custom modules.",
      "most_likely_effort": 6
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "U6: Job orchestration documentation",
      "activity_description": "Write the 'job orchestration' section of the reference guide: outline, composed batch workflow examples using the DSL, explanatory text, and editorial review/polish.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "U7: Add undeployed status to YARN SPI",
      "activity_description": "Add the UNDEPLOYED state to the YARN SPI status model, update YARN application-state-to-status mapping so undeployed applications report UNDEPLOYED instead of UNKNOWN, and add unit tests for the mapping.",
      "most_likely_effort": 2
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "U8: Split admin artifact per Hadoop distribution",
      "activity_description": "Restructure the build into a common admin core plus per-distro admin modules, scope Hadoop-distro-specific dependencies to their modules, update packaging and CI configuration, and verify each distro-specific assembly builds and starts correctly.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Cross-module integration, system testing, and release support",
      "activity_description": "Run end-to-end integration tests across the modified modules, update CI pipelines for the new module structure, fix integration defects, and prepare release notes for the increment.",
      "most_likely_effort": 4
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 39
  }
}

Let me analyze this specification. It appears to be about the Spring Framework, specifically referencing "Flo" (Spring Cloud Data Flow's Flo DSL for stream definitions), Spring Integration (SI), JobLaunchingTasklet (Spring Cloud Task / Spring Batch), YARN SPI (Spring Cloud Data Flow YARN), SpEL expressions, and admin artifacts with Hadoop distro libraries. This looks like an increment of Spring Cloud Data Flow development.

Let me break down the user stories:

U1: Add `timeout` and `pollInterval` as global options at the DSL level in Flo — so users can override defaults. This involves DSL parser changes, option propagation, tests.

U2: Upgrade to Spring Integration 4.2.1 release — dependency upgrade, testing for regressions.

U3: Review and refactor JobLaunchingTasklet to improve performance — code review, profiling, refactoring, tests.

U4: Enhance test coverage to capture DSL and XML generation variants — writing tests for DSL and XML generation.

U5: Use SpEL expressions inline at stream definition level — parser changes to support SpEL in stream definitions, evaluation context, tests.

U6: Documentation for 'job orchestration' — writing docs.

U7: Add `undeployed` status for YARN SPI — add enum/status value, mapping logic, tests.

U8: Split `admin` artifact packaged with hadoop distro specific libraries — build refactoring, Maven/Gradle module split, distribution packaging.

I need to estimate effort in workdays for each activity using WBS-based estimation.

Let me define activities:

1. Requirements analysis & design (overall increment planning, design decisions for DSL global options, SpEL support) — maybe per story design.
2. U1: Implement global timeout/pollInterval options in Flo DSL (parser, options propagation, unit tests).
3. U2: Upgrade Spring Integration to 4.2.1 (dependency bump, resolve API changes, regression testing).
4. U3: Review & refactor JobLaunchingTasklet (profiling, refactor, tests).
5. U4: Enhance test coverage for DSL and XML generation variants.
6. U5: Support inline SpEL expressions at stream definition level (parser changes, evaluation, security/context handling, tests).
7. U6: Write job orchestration documentation.
8. U7: Add `undeployed` status to YARN SPI (status enum, mapping, tests).
9. U8: Split admin artifact per Hadoop distro (build refactoring, packaging, verification).
10. Integration, system testing & release (integration tests across modules, CI updates, release notes).

Plus maybe code review/QA activities. Let me assign effort estimates.

Technical and design decisions:
- Java 17+ with Spring Framework 6? Wait, the spec mentions Spring Framework 6.0 requires Java 17+. But the user stories mention SI 4.2.1, which is old (Spring Integration 4.2.1 is from 2015). There's an inconsistency. Actually, this spec appears to be from Spring Cloud Data Flow's early days (2015). The intro about Spring Framework 6.0 is generic. Hmm. I should make assumptions: The increment targets the existing Spring Cloud Data Flow codebase (Java-based, Spring Boot, Spring Integration, Spring Batch, YARN SPI). Assume compatibility matrix is defined; the SI 4.2.1 upgrade implies the codebase is on Spring Integration 4.x line, so I'll assume the project is on the corresponding Spring Framework 4.x line despite the generic intro, OR treat the intro as background and the stories as the actual increment. To be safe, I'll note the assumption that the codebase is Spring Cloud Data Flow (Flo DSL, Spring Batch, Spring Cloud Deployer YARN) built with Maven, Java 8-era Spring Integration 4.x line, and that the intro is contextual background. Actually, the instruction says: "If the specification does not contain information that you consider necessary, make a reasonable assumption and record it." So I can record the assumption.

Design decisions:
- U1: Add `timeout` and `pollInterval` as global options in the Flo DSL parser; store in stream definition metadata; propagate to runtime as deployment properties; maintain backward compatibility with defaults.
- U5: Extend the DSL parser to recognize inline SpEL expressions (e.g., `{{ ... }}` or standard `#{}` syntax) at stream definition level; evaluate via a shared StandardEvaluationContext; ensure works with OOTB and custom modules.
- U7: Extend Status/DeploymentState enum in YARN SPI with `undeployed`; map YARN application states accordingly; replace `unknown` mapping.
- U8: Restructure build: create per-distro admin modules (e.g., admin-hdp, admin-cdh, admin-phd) with a common core; use Maven profiles/dependency management.
- U2: Bump SI version in dependency management; run full regression.
- U3: Profile JobLaunchingTasklet; refactor to reduce overhead (e.g., avoid redundant job repository queries, optimize parameter handling).
- U4: Parameterized tests for DSL and XML config generation variants.
- U6: Asciidoc reference docs for job orchestration.

Assumptions:
- Single developer (myself) performing all work.
- Workday = 8 hours of productive effort.
- Existing codebase with CI (Maven), existing test infrastructure.
- No clarifications needed; scope limited to the listed stories.
- Documentation in Asciidoc within the reference guide.
- The estimate excludes PM overhead, meetings beyond development, and ops.
- Estimates include unit tests but integration/system testing is a separate activity.

Effort estimates (workdays):

1. Increment analysis & design (A1): 3 days. Analyze stories, design DSL parser changes, SpEL integration approach, YARN status mapping, build restructure plan.

2. U1 implementation (A2): 4 days. Parser changes (2), option propagation & defaults handling (1), unit tests (1).

3. U2 SI 4.2.1 upgrade (A3): 3 days. Dependency bump & conflict resolution (1), adapt code to API changes (1), regression verification (1).

4. U3 JobLaunchingTasklet review & refactor (A4): 5 days. Profiling/analysis (1.5), refactoring (2.5), unit/integration tests (1).

5. U4 Test coverage for DSL and XML generation variants (A5): 4 days. Identify variant matrix (1), implement parameterized tests (2.5), stabilize (0.5).

6. U5 Inline SpEL at stream definition level (A6): 6 days. Parser support (2), evaluation context & validation (2), tests incl. custom modules (1.5), security/edge cases (0.5). SpEL in DSL is a significant feature.

7. U6 Job orchestration documentation (A7): 3 days. Outline & examples (1), writing (1.5), review/polish (0.5).

8. U7 YARN SPI undeployed status (A8): 2 days. Enum/model change & mapping (1), tests (0.5), verification (0.5).

9. U8 Split admin artifact per Hadoop distro (A9): 5 days. Module structure design (1), build/dependency refactor (2), packaging & CI updates (1), verification of each distro assembly (1).

10. Integration, system testing & release support (A10): 4 days. End-to-end integration tests (2), CI pipeline updates (1), release notes & defect fixes buffer (1).

technical_and_design_decisions: Target the existing Spring Cloud Data Flow codebase (Flo DSL parser, Spring Batch integration, Spring Cloud Deployer YARN SPI, Maven multi-module build) since the user stories reference Flo, SI, JobLaunchingTasklet, YARN SPI, and admin artifacts.

U1: Extend the Flo DSL parser to accept 'timeout' and 'pollInterval' as global stream-level options, persist them in the stream definition metadata, and propagate them as deployment properties at runtime while keeping existing defaults for backward compatibility.
U2: Perform the Spring Integration 4.2.1 upgrade through the central dependency management (Maven BOM), resolving any API/behavior changes and validating via the existing regression suite.

U3: Profile JobLaunchingTasklet first to identify hot spots (e.g., redundant JobRepository lookups, repeated parameter conversion), then refactor internals without changing its public contract, keeping existing job-launch semantics intact.
U4: Implement parameterized/data-driven tests that enumerate DSL variants and generated Spring XML configuration variants so both generation paths are covered by a shared test matrix.

U5: Extend the stream definition DSL grammar to recognize inline SpEL expressions and evaluate them through a shared, hardened StandardEvaluationContext so the feature works uniformly for out-of-the-box and custom modules.

assumptions: All work is performed by a single developer (the author) with no parallelization; estimates are effort, not elapsed duration.

Per-activity estimates include design, implementation, and unit testing for that activity; cross-module integration/system testing and release activities are estimated as a separate activity.

Scope is limited to the eight user stories; project management, stakeholder meetings, and operational deployment work are excluded.

No clarifying questions are needed; any ambiguity is resolved by the reasonable interpretations stated here.
